Karoon Outlines Lower-Cost Neon Project Development, Proceeds to FEED
By David Winning
SYDNEY--Karoon Energy outlined a new development plan for its offshore Neon project in Brazil, which reduces costs and could lead to maiden crude-oil production in 2030.
Karoon now estimates capital costs from a development of Neon of between US$800 million and US$950 million. That is lower than the US$900 million-U$1.2 billion estimated in April 2025.

Karoon said early design and engineering work would begin on a first phase of the project, which is located around 47 miles northeast of its existing Bauna project and aims to produce 25,000-30,000 barrels of oil at its peak.
"There are also opportunities for future development phases, which will leverage the initial infrastructure investment," said Carri Lockhart, Karoon's chief executive and managing director.
Karoon estimated an internal rate of return in a mid-20% range, which assumes a long-term Brent crude-oil price of US$73.50 a barrel.
It is targeting a final investment decision on Karoon in the second half of 2027, which hinges on the sale of a 30-50% interest in the project to a strategic partner.

"Sharing the development risk and capital would reduce Karoon's concentration of capital in a single project and preserve capacity to invest across other accretive growth opportunities," Lockhart said.
